title: The window and your data
summary: Around the Canvas is worfy's window: the Command palette (⌘K), the menu, Settings, and notifications when a Session or a Ticket needs you. It is light or dark as the system is. worfy keeps its own state in a data folder on this Machine, and reads Tickets, ADRs and transcripts where they lie.

scene.description: The window and your data. On the left, what worfy reads where it lies: the workflow files, Tickets, HANDOFF and ADRs, from which a Ticket on the Canvas is read; and Claude home, from whose transcripts a Session's conversation is read. In the middle, the window: the Command palette and the menu, which both open Settings; a toast; and the Canvas with a Ticket and a Session. On the right, outside the window: the data folder, where Settings and each Canvas's Layout, Cards and trash are saved and where a renderer or helper process that ended leaves a line in logs/; and the system notification, which a Session or a Ticket that needs you raises. The Canvas's automatic archive shows a toast with Undo.

labels.toastNote: a short message in the window
labels.notificationNote: when worfy is not in front
labels.step1: ⌘K opens the Command palette: it finds commands and things of the Project and runs them. The palette and the menu open Settings, worfy's own settings on this Machine.
labels.step2: worfy keeps its own state in one data folder on this Machine: the Project list, Settings, and each Project's Layout, Cards and trash. None of it goes into the Project's repository.
labels.step3: Tickets, HANDOFF, ADRs and transcripts are not in that folder: worfy reads them where they lie.
labels.step4: While no worfy window has focus, a system notification says that a Session finished its turn or needs your answer, or that a Ticket waits for you. Inside the window, toasts give short messages.
labels.step5: If worfy cannot start, a window and stderr name the step that failed and what to try. A renderer or helper process that ended leaves a line in logs/ of the data folder.

flow.description: The data flow of Settings, notifications and the memory figure. In the renderer: the Settings window, the renderer copy of the settings, NotificationTarget and the memory figure. In the main process: the settings store, the SessionRegistry, the Notifier and the MemorySampler. On the side of the disk and the system: the data folder and the system notification. The Settings window sends a change on appSettings.set to the store, which writes it to the data folder through a temporary file and a rename, and sends appSettings.changed to the renderer copy of every window, which gives the window the newest state. The SessionRegistry passes a Session's result, permission request or question to the Notifier, which shows a system notification; its click comes back to the Notifier, which sends notify.open to NotificationTarget. The memory figure opens the MemorySampler with memory.open and gets each sample on memory.changed.

text: The data folder is worfy for a packaged build and worfy-dev for a development build, so both run at once; WORFY_DATA_DIR overrides it. A second start over a folder in use quits.
Most JSON state files that do not parse or match their schema are set aside as <name>.unreadable-<time>, not overwritten, and that part of worfy starts empty.

files.src/main/storage/json-file.ts: Read with a schema, set-aside, atomic write
files.src/renderer/palette/commands.ts: The palette's commands, from the window's state
files.src/main/startup-failure.ts: The steps of the start; the failed-start window

limits: No notification of a Session or a Ticket while a worfy window has focus; at most one per Session in 10 seconds.
At most 3 toasts are on screen; info and success toasts hide after 4 seconds.
Entries older than 3 days leave each Project's trash when the app starts.
